Find the measure of angle $C$ given that $m∠A=m∠B.$

$m∠C=$
{{field-1}}${}^{∘}$
question.worked_solution:
Using $m∠A=m∠B,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠A & =m∠B \\ 8w-{2}^{∘} & =9w-{10}^{∘} \\ w & ={8}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, substituting $w={8}^{∘}$ in the expression for $m∠A,$ we get

$$
m∠A=8({8}^{∘})-{2}^{∘}={62}^{∘}.
$$

Now, we can find $m∠C$ using the fact that the internal angles of any triangle sum to ${180}^{∘}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠A+m∠B+m∠C & ={180}^{∘} \\ 2m∠A+m∠C & ={180}^{∘} \\ 2\cdot {62}^{∘}+m∠C & ={180}^{∘} \\ {124}^{∘}+m∠C & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠C & ={56}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$
